Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this task changes a multi-wake dogfish target policy; I’ll inspect its required keyframes before proposing the single candidate. I’ll first read the workspace contract and then trace the assigned parent, inherited evidence, and sampled results.

The inherited evidence spans four sampled rollouts: two successful controller behaviors (one duplicated result) and one domain-exit failure. I’m anchoring the visual sheets to their trajectory/load metrics and controller implementations before choosing the mutation; the key comparison will be the fastest successful rollout versus the informative failure, with the assigned parent as the baseline.

The direct sibling comparison is unusually clean: changing only the bounded positive-bearing steering pair from `0.55/8°` to `0.70/10°` cut capture time from `130.23` to `91.61`, mean distance from `3.516L` to `2.834L`, and peak lateral offset from `5.425L` to `4.297L`. The rate-lead variant, despite retaining the same gait, reversed that gain into a right-domain exit. I’m recording that diagnosis now, before touching the policy as required by the visual-evidence skill.

The candidate now adopts only the proven `0.70/10°` steering pair and leaves the successful propulsion package unchanged. The durable guidance records both the measured improvement and its load boundary, plus the rate-lead failure as an explicit avoid/test condition. I’m moving to the mandated non-CFD contract, schema, guidance-delta, and edit-boundary checks.

The first mandated check exposed a rendered-workspace defect rather than a candidate defect: `README.md` contains the same “copied to guidance” parent line twice, so the checker counts two markers although both name the identical parent. I’m inspecting the checker’s parent-resolution rule and will make the smallest in-workspace repair needed to let the required semantic guidance comparison run.

The guidance check now passes after removing the duplicated parent marker. The Julia contract command itself could not start because this workspace image has no `julia` on its login-shell `PATH` (the policy did not execute or fail an assertion). I’m checking the pinned environment for an available Julia binary, then I’ll run the boundary guard independently as required.

Implemented exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl): adopts the evidence-backed `0.70` steering gain and `10°` limit while preserving the successful gait.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md): records visual diagnosis, metrics, hypothesis, and falsification boundaries.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md): adds the reusable steering improvement and bearing-rate failure lesson.

All mandated checks pass: guidance semantic delta, Julia policy contract/finite action, and solver edit boundary. I also removed a duplicate assigned-parent marker from `README.md` that initially prevented the guidance checker from resolving its parent. No CFD was run.
